pairs.difference: A: the telescope stands whole on its tripod with a thin diagonal tube and thin legs. Subject area is 0.203, below the real 0.233 floor, so at thumbnail the background stripes and grey ground take most of the card. B: the binoculars are a chunky mass filling the card width (margin 0.04) and read instantly at thumbnail.
pairs.fix: Move in close on the telescope so the large gold-rimmed front lens and thick barrel dominate the card, with the barrel running nearly edge to edge and the tripod partly cut off by the bottom edge.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is a tall form filling 0.833 of the height, with the gold badge at dead centre as a clear focal point. B: the meteor sits centred as a complete ball with a flame trail to the upper right. The flame takes up width but adds little mass, and the rock reads as a brown lump before it reads as a meteor. Both measurements are in range, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Draw the meteor larger and on a steeper diagonal, with the rock nearly touching the lower left and a thick flame trail running off the top right corner.

pairs.difference: A: one huge tilted dish fills the top of the card and pushes close to the top and left edges, while the base is centred below. It is a complete object posed on empty dunes. B: the sandcastle shows several towers plus a bucket and shovel, a more crowded read but seated in the scene. Both are in range, and A reads bolder, so the vector gives only a weak lean toward A from the placed-in-the-middle, nothing-cropped staging.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera lower and closer so the dish rim runs off the top right edge and the base sits cut off by the bottom edge.

pairs.difference: A: the rover is fully contained with a 0.095 margin, close to the real ceiling. The dish and solar panel stack upward into a busy top, so at thumbnail the white dish competes with the orange body. B: the taxi spans the card (width 0.926, margin 0.035) on a three-quarter road angle, with one clear mass and an instant read.
pairs.fix: Draw the rover bigger and at a stronger three-quarter angle so it spans almost the full card width, and shrink the dish so the orange body is seen first.

pairs.difference: A: the two sneakers sit low and wide on a two-tone floor and wall, close to the side edge (margin 0.033), with box height 0.487 under the real range. B: the helmet is a single centred object with a 0.149 margin, well above the real 0.108 ceiling. That even band of empty pink around it matches the lessons' pulled-back generated framing.
pairs.fix: Enlarge the helmet until it nearly touches the card sides, tilted slightly to one side, with less empty floor below it.

pairs.difference: A: the pool is a wide oval nearly touching both sides (width 0.94, margin 0.023), set in a garden corner, and the duck gives it a clear centre. B: the jacket floats centred on a sunburst with moderate margins, and the sash reads first. Both framings match real cards: the wide scene crop and the floating object on a burst. Nothing in the framing separates them.

A: the bar scene is cropped by the top and right edges, with the roof and counter running off the card. This cut-in framing matches the real lighthouse, bike and Ferris wheel cards. B: the dome sits whole and small in the middle, with its tube attached and a wide band of empty grey ground below. The lower third is dead space, and at thumbnail the object is a small pale shape.
pairs.fix: Move in close on the dome so it fills the card, with the side tube cut off by the right edge and the ground strip reduced to a thin band at the bottom.

pairs.difference: A: the planet is dead centre with a bright halo behind it, and the ring is the only thing spreading to the sides, so box height is 0.533 under the real range. The glow around the hero matches the generated glove and camera lessons. B: the two sandals sit on a diagonal, offset and overlapping in depth, with a simple stripe ground and no halo.
pairs.fix: Remove the glow behind the planet. Draw the sphere larger, off-centre and tilted, with the ring cut off by the card edge.

pairs.difference: A: the book is cropped by the card (margin 0, width 1.0) with a railing and pot in the corners. This is an in-scene framing that real cards use, though the pot and foliage add some competing detail. B: the chair is a thin frame with subject area 0.202, below the real 0.237 floor, but the green seat and back still read first and it stands clearly on a plain ground. The thin build explains the low area, and neither framing is out of line with real cards.

A: the player sits off-centre upper left, with cables looping to the earbuds at lower right. This is an asymmetric diagonal layout with the hero broken into a main block and secondary pieces. B: the saucer is level, symmetrical and dead centre on concentric rings, with height 0.467 under the real range and width 0.905 above it, so it is a flat strip across the middle with empty yellow above and below.
pairs.fix: Tilt the saucer steeply toward the viewer and draw it larger, so the green dome and the underside both show and it fills more of the card height.

pairs.difference: A: the cart fills the height (0.869) with a strong red and white awning at the top, a clear name-at-a-glance silhouette, seated on a paved ground. B: the panel is a squat block in the lower middle with a blank patterned wall above and an empty grey floor below. At thumbnail the two rows of small buttons compete with each other and the object is harder to name.
pairs.fix: Draw the control panel larger and from a lower angle so it fills the card top to bottom, with the lever reaching near the top edge and three or four big buttons instead of two small rows.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket is a complete object on a clean diagonal centred on a sunburst, with a 0.11 margin at the top of the real range and subject area 0.252 on the low side, so there is a wide even clearance all round. B: the submarine is a heavier mass (0.324) that reads faster, with a periscope breaking the upper silhouette. Both are clean reads, so the lean rests on A's slimmer hero and larger clearance.
pairs.fix: Draw the rocket fatter and larger so the nose nearly touches the top edge and the fins nearly touch the bottom and left edges.

pattern: Generated cards show the whole object, centred and fully inside the card, with an even band of empty space around it. Real cards more often get cropped by an edge, cut into a scene, or sit off-centre on a diagonal. The lessons show the same drift: the generated lighthouse pulls back to show its full base on a rock island where the real one is cut off by the bottom edge. Other tells are halos behind the hero (planet here, glove in the lessons), empty floor bands below the object (dome, panel), and thin or flat heroes at the edge of the real occupancy range (telescope, saucer). Caveat: most measurements are in range, so this vector alone is weak. Some calls were also influenced by subject matter: the review folder is named sci-fi and many A/B picks are space objects. That is not composition evidence, and p02, p03 and p12 in particular rest more on it than on framing. p09's neither is also partly subject-based: the chair's camp emblem matches the scarf and jacket, despite its below-range area.
